vulnerability.name: CORS Misconfiguration
vulnerability.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing configuration vulnerabilities that expose sensitive data
vulnerability.impact: Cross-origin data theft, credential hijacking, or unauthorized API access
vulnerability.mitigation: Use specific origins in CORS policies, avoid wildcards with credentials, validate origins properly

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The provided Solidity contract does not have a Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) configuration, but this vulnerability is not applicable to Ethereum smart contracts since CORS is an HTTP-level security mechanism.
findings.remediation: CORS is not relevant for Ethereum smart contracts.

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The Solidity contract does not have a CORS configuration, which may expose sensitive data if called from another origin.
findings.impact: Cross-origin data theft or unauthorized API access
findings.entry_point: All functions of the SimpleDAO contract
findings.execution_path_diagram:
```
SimpleDAO -> Called from another origin without CORS check
```
exploitation_steps: Call the SimpleDAO contract from another origin
Interact with the contract (e.g., donate or withdraw functions)
findings.exploitation_conditions: Another origin can call the Solidity contract
findings.remediation: Ensure that the Solidity contract has a proper CORS configuration to restrict calls to specific origins.

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The vulnerable code uses `hasNoBalance` before `supportsToken`, which can potentially allow an attacker to exploit the reentrancy vulnerability.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
```
1. Attacker calls airDrop() > 2. Contract calls hasNoBalance() (invalid) > 3. Contract calls supportsToken() > 4. Reentrancy attack occurs```
exploitation_steps: Attacker exploits reentrancy vulnerability by calling into the contract during the hasNoBalance validation
findings.exploitation_conditions: An attacker can call the airDrop function and manipulate the contract state
findings.remediation: Ensure that `supportsToken` is always evaluated before any action that depends on it in the contract
